1_parties_and_buyer_credit.value: Seller is Havrebakke Vind ApS. Buyer is Jutland Board & Packaging A/S, which is unrated. The Buyer's payment obligations are guaranteed by its parent, Jutland Industri Holding A/S, through a parent company guarantee (Annex 4). No rating trigger is mentioned.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.quote: Payment obligations guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.clause: Part I; Part II 9.2; Annex 4 (as cited in the summary's Key terms table)
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.note: This document is counsel's due diligence summary, not the PPA. Clause references are the summary's own. The summary says the parent guarantee is the credit the committee relies on and recommends reviewing the guarantor's last three years of accounts. The guarantee wording itself (Annex 4) is not reproduced.

2_facility.value: Eight onshore wind turbines with 48.0 MW capacity at Havrebakke, Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, in bidding zone DK1. The country is Denmark (the summary describes Danish law and Danish onshore wind).
2_facility.quote: Eight onshore turbines, 48.0 MW, Havrebakke, Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, DK1.
2_facility.note: The summary gives a single 48.0 MW figure and does not say whether it is AC or DC.

3_supply_period.value: The Supply Period is ten years and starts on the Commercial Operation Date.
3_supply_period.quote: The Supply Period runs ten (10) years from the Commercial Operation Date.

4_cod_and_delay.value: Target COD is 1 October 2027 and the Longstop Date is 31 March 2028. Delay damages are EUR 9,600 per day after the Target COD, capped at EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.quote: Target COD 1 October 2027. Longstop Date 31 March 2028. Delay damages EUR 9,600 per day after the Target COD, capped at EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.note: Failure to reach COD by the Longstop Date is also listed as an Event of Default (Part II 12–13).

5_price_and_indexation.value: The price is EUR 54.50 per MWh, stated in the Election Sheet. Thirty per cent of the price is adjusted annually by the Danish consumer price index, starting 1 January 2029.
5_price_and_indexation.quote: EUR 54.50 per MWh per the Election Sheet. Thirty per cent of the price is adjusted annually from 1 January 2029 by the Danish consumer price index.
5_price_and_indexation.clause: Part II 7.1; Annex 2 (price taken from the Election Sheet)
5_price_and_indexation.note: The summary lists Annex 2 as a reference for this term but does not say in terms that Annex 2 is the Election Sheet.

6_volume_and_performance.value: Pay-as-produced: the Buyer takes 100 % of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production is 158,000 MWh (P50). Minimum Annual Production is 118,500 MWh, with a shortfall payment as the remedy.
6_volume_and_performance.quote: 100 % of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production 158,000 MWh (P50). Minimum Annual Production 118,500 MWh with a shortfall payment.
6_volume_and_performance.note: How the shortfall payment is calculated is not stated in the summary. The pay-as-produced characterisation comes from Section 1 of the summary.

7_product_and_certificates.value: The Seller sells electricity and all Guarantees of Origin, which are transferred at no additional cost. No capacity product is sold.
7_product_and_certificates.quote: Electricity and all Guarantees of Origin, transferred at no additional cost.
7_product_and_certificates.note: No volume or price is given for the Guarantees of Origin, only that they pass at no additional cost.

8_curtailment.value: The Buyer may instruct reductions for up to 150 hours per Contract Year, paid as Deemed Delivered Electricity at the Contract Price. Reductions instructed by the transmission system operator are not compensated by the Buyer.
8_curtailment.quote: Buyer may instruct reductions for up to 150 hours per Contract Year, paid as Deemed Delivered Electricity at the Contract Price. Reductions instructed by the transmission system operator are not compensated by the Buyer.
8_curtailment.note: The cap is stated in hours only, with no MWh cap. The summary says the Seller has no equivalent curtailment right and that 150 hours is at the upper end of market practice. The summary does not mention treatment of negative prices.

9_delivery_point_and_balancing.value: Physical delivery at the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation. The Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears imbalance costs from COD. No financial reference price applies because settlement is physical.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.quote: Physical delivery at the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation. Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears imbalance costs from COD.

10_credit_support.value: Seller: bank guarantee of EUR 2,000,000 from Financial Close until twelve months after COD. Buyer: a parent company guarantee plus a letter of credit equal to nine months of expected payments.
10_credit_support.quote: Seller: bank guarantee EUR 2,000,000 from Financial Close until twelve months after COD. Buyer: parent company guarantee plus a letter of credit equal to nine months of expected payments.
10_credit_support.note: The Buyer's letter of credit is sized as nine months of expected payments, with no EUR amount given. The duration of the Buyer's credit support is not stated.

11_default_and_termination.value: Events of Default include non-payment within ten Business Days of notice, insolvency, and failure to reach COD by the Longstop Date. The Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remaining Supply Period.
11_default_and_termination.quote: Non-payment within ten Business Days of notice, insolvency and failure to reach COD by the Longstop Date are Events of Default. Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remaining Supply Period.
11_default_and_termination.note: The calculation method is stated, but this document does not name the source of the Reference Forward Price. Counsel says the agreement names it and that it is a published DK1 forward curve (Section 3, point 4). The discount rate is not stated. The list of Events of Default may not be exhaustive.

12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.value: A cost impact from Change in Law above EUR 250,000 in a Contract Year triggers good-faith renegotiation. If there is no agreement within 90 days, the affected Party may terminate without a Termination Amount. Force majeure lasting more than 180 consecutive days gives either Party a termination right.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.quote: Change in Law is a defined term. A cost impact above EUR 250,000 in a Contract Year triggers good-faith renegotiation; absent agreement within 90 days the affected Party may terminate without a Termination Amount. Force majeure beyond 180 consecutive days gives either Party a termination right.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.clause: Part II 11 (change in law), Part II 10 (force majeure)
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.note: The summary does not say which Party bears the cost of a change in law beyond the renegotiation and termination mechanism. Counsel notes the termination right is mutual and that lenders are expected to ask for it to be tightened, with a lender consent letter likely required at Financial Close.
